concept: llama.cpp seq_pos_min hybrid memory fix PR 24797
summary: Master still reads `seq_pos_min` as `std::max(mem_attn->seq_pos_min(seq_id), mem_recr->seq_pos_min(seq_id))` with the comment "the min of the total cache is the max of the two caches' min values", and `seq_pos_max` as the `std::min` of both.

facts.text: Master still reads `seq_pos_min` as `std::max(mem_attn->seq_pos_min(seq_id), mem_recr->seq_pos_min(seq_id))` with the comment "the min of the total cache is the max of the two caches' min values", and `seq_pos_max` as the `std::min` of both.
The reason ggerganov gave for rejecting the change: "the recurrent state is valid only for the latest position and using it with any other position is incorrect".
The rejected change also let a rollback that exceeded `n_rs_seq` fall through to normal cell removal, which keeps attention KV trimmed but leaves a recurrent state at the wrong position.

The replacement PR 25592 states the invariant instead: recurrent state is only restored at the exact position it was saved at. It records checkpoint validity at save time (`pos_min = pos_max` for hybrid and recurrent memory), restores a checkpoint only when its exact position lies inside the common prefix of the new prompt, and erases checkpoints that cover diverged content instead of trimming them.
PR 25592 makes no change to `llama_memory_hybrid`; `seq_rm` still fails cleanly on impossible rollbacks, now with a debug log.

The master server code carries the open marker: `[TAG_CHECKPOINTS_FIX_POS_MIN]` TODO "here we incorrectly determine that the saved checkpoint data covers the [pos_min, pos_max] range", plus a restore-side workaround that rejects a checkpoint with `pos_max > pos_next`.

PR 24110 changed `pos_min_thold` so the `-1` margin applies only when no new tokens exist (`has_new_tokens = n_past < task.n_tokens()`); this avoids restoring a checkpoint when the slot already holds the prefix. Master has it.

2026-06-19: PR 24797 opened. 2026-06-26/27: a tester reports most invalidations gone on b9820 with the patch, still seeing `clearing stale recurrent state beyond n_past = 10047 (recr_pos_max = 15932)` under many parallel sessions.
2026-06-27: ggerganov calls the change "obviously wrong" and closes the PR.
2026-07-12: krim404 opens PR 25592 as "a reimplementation of #24797" and states that 24797 "was rejected because it could reuse recurrent state at positions it was never valid for".

2026-07-14: the PR is rebased after PRs 25472 and 25649 landed; a second commit drops the bounded `n_rs_seq` rollback fast path because those snapshots are valid only for tokens decoded in the last ubatch.
2026-07 to 2026-08: testers report 150 to 400 times faster turns on restored checkpoints; the newest comment on the cached page is dated 2026-08-26 and no merge event appears.

Speculative decoding can loop on hybrid models: PR 25819 (WIP mitigation, 2026-07-17) logs `STUCK speculative loop: 4 consecutive checkpoint restores with no progress` for ngram-mod drafts after a restore. A 2026-08-25 commenter says the bug "happens often enough to be noticeable" with 25592 and 26004.
PR 24785, a different approach (recurrent shrink/expand ported from BeeLlama), was also proposed for the same symptoms.

Contributor view: the max() inflates `pos_min`, so the fix is to report the attention minimum. Maintainer view: positions other than the latest are invalid for recurrent state, so the fix belongs in checkpoint metadata and restore rules. They disagree on where the invariant is enforced; the maintainer view decided the outcome.

Testers of 24797 reported working caches; the closure reason says the cache hits could rest on invalid state. Whether any corruption occurred is unmeasured; 25592 reports byte-identical output at temperature 0 against a cold prefill.
Whether PR 25592 merges, and whether upstream adopts its `pos_min = pos_max` bookkeeping or a different one.
Whether Metal behaves like the CUDA, ROCm and Vulkan logs; every cited test is on those backends.
PR 24797 was closed by ggerganov on 2026-06-27 and is not merged.
ggerganov's closing comment is "This change is obviously wrong - the recurrent state is valid only for the latest position and using it with any other position is incorrect."
Master `llama_memory_hybrid::seq_pos_min` still returns the max of the attention and recurrent minimums.
PR 25592 describes itself as a reimplementation of 24797 that keeps the exact-position invariant.
PR 25592 resolves the `[TAG_CHECKPOINTS_FIX_POS_MIN]` TODO for hybrid and recurrent memory.
PR 25592 logs checkpoint create, restore and erase at INFO so they show without `-lv`.
PR 25592's author tested on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M on Vulkan; a repeated 22.8k-token request went from about 96 s to a 4-token cache hit.
A tester on an RTX 3090 with Qwen3.8-27B IQ4_NL measured a 38.5K-token prefill of 40.8 s falling to 0.1 to 0.3 s after restore.
A third-party report says reusing an equivalent checkpoint instead of saving a new one cut a 1156-token warm request from about 122 ms to 43 ms on a Radeon 780M.
Issue 22746 (Qwen 3.6 27B full re-processing, opened 2026-05-06) is marked Closed.
Issue 23589 traced a cache drop of one batch (`-b`) worth of tokens per turn to commit ccee426 (PR 23280).
The author of PR 24110 said it might also fix issue 23589, and ggerganov called the change technically correct but asked for a repro on master.
